subject: Annual billing migration: safeguards, deferred discounts, and ramp cadence
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Annual billing migration — exploring options and guardrails

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. The execs are pushing us to move to annual prepay for 2027 but they want to preserve flex for the first 6 months — specifically:

- A safety net if usage exceeds the committed tranche (surge pooling / on-demand top-up)
- A modest runway of credits if we miss the ramp assumptions in Q1/Q2
- Clear SLA credits tied to latency and availability in the first 90 days

Can Redwood support a migration from our current monthly invoicing to an annual prepay with a deferred-discount structure (apply discount fully after 6 months subject to true-up)? Also need to understand how overage/top-up pricing would work.

If you could send a short proposal with line items (year 1 committed spend, discount tiers, true-up cadence, and any SLA exceptions) we can circulate to procurement.

Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Health

Acme Health (procurement@acmehealth.com)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Annual billing migration — exploring options and guardrails

Jordan — thanks, this is helpful context. Attached is a concise proposal (Redwood_Annual_Offer_v3.pdf) and an SLA exceptions workbook we typically use when a customer wants staged concessions. High level summary here:

- Offer: 12-month prepaid commitment with a 30% discount applied at signing on the committed tranche.
- Deferred discount: additional 5% credit applied after a 6-month true-up if actual usage is within ±15% of forecast. If usage is >115%, customer pays overage at the pre-discount rate (on-demand), with a surge top-up option priced at 25% above prepay unit cost for immediate capacity.
- Ramp protections: 3-month staged true-ups (monthly telemetry, 3-month cumulative true-up) with a one-time safety credit (equal to 2% of committed spend) if utilization is <70% at the 6-month check and customer triggers the safety net.
- SLA: standard 99.9% monthly uptime. For first 90 days, we can provide enhanced credits for latency SLO misses up to a 5% rebate (requires approval). Details in SLA-exceptions.xlsx.

Questions for procurement: will you accept a single-signature DocuSign for the commercial terms, or does procurement require a PO + counter-signed agreement?

I looped in Karthik (solutions) and Ben (commercial) to confirm the surge/top-up pricing and approval path.

Thanks — I can be flexible on the true-up cadence if procurement needs quota-alignment to fiscal quarters.

- Vanessa

Subject: Re: Annual billing migration — technical/ops notes

Vanessa / Ben — quick notes from infra side that should go in the commercial appendix: 

1) Surge/top-up: implement as a short-lived on-demand capacity SKU (30-minute min) billed at +25% of list token cost, with a soft cap alert when spend on surge >10% of committed monthly tranche. This keeps burst protection without large financial tail risk.

2) Prefix/KV cache warmup: for a first-quarter onboarding, we recommend a 2-week pre-warm window where the customer can run higher-cost warmup jobs at no charge (incentivizes performance). Cap that at $3k of compute.

3) True-up telemetry: we will provide a monthly usage CSV and a consolidated 3-month report for the 6-month true-up. Suggest aligning the true-up to the nearest fiscal quarter-end to simplify procurement.

4) SLA credits: the enhanced 90-day credits are feasible but require sales leadership sign-off for anything beyond 5% rebate.

I attached a sample SLA-exceptions.xlsx tab layout.

—Karthik

Subject: Revised commercial — annual prepay with staged discount and surge terms

Jordan — following internal approvals, here's a clean commercial summary you can share with procurement: 

- Year 1 committed spend: $600,000 prepaid at signing (12-month term)
- Upfront discount: 30% applied to committed tranche on signing
- Deferred credit: additional 5% credit applied at the 6-month true-up if usage within ±15% of forecast. Credit appears as a contra-charge on the next invoice or as a one-time credit if contract continues.
- Surge/top-up: on-demand SKU priced at 25% above prepay unit cost; 30-minute minimum; automated alerts if surge spending exceeds 10% of monthly committed tranche.
- Safety credit: one-time $12,000 safety credit (2% of committed spend) eligible at 6-month true-up if utilization <70% and customer requests the safety net.
- SLA: standard 99.9% uptime; enhanced 90-day latency credit up to 5% of monthly invoice for SLO failures (requires counterparty sign-off).

I've uploaded the offer to DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/ACME-2026-annual-offer. We'll follow a PO + signature flow if that's required on your side — happy to accommodate.

Attachments: Redwood_Annual_Offer_v3.pdf, SLA-exceptions.xlsx

Next steps: if procurement confirms the PO flow, we'll issue a final contract with the above commercial terms and DocuSign for the signature. If they'd prefer the credit applied differently (e.g., true-up rebate instead of contra-charge), call that out and we can adjust the contract language.

Best,
